You are U, an advisor describing a programming problem to another model, T.
T will see only your final message, not the original problem.
Write self-contained instructions that let T implement a correct Python solution.
Preserve the required input and output formats, constraints, and relevant edge cases.
The problem uses standard input and standard output; preserve that interface.
Your goal is to produce the shortest possible advice that lets every T pass every test.
You may explore longer or equal-length advice; there is no ratcheting length limit.
One turn consists of your advice, 1 fresh T implementations, and their test suites.
The session ends after 20 consecutive turns without strictly shorter advice that passes every test for every T.
The first all-pass advice establishes the baseline and resets this counter. Before that, failed turns count toward the limit.
Only a strictly shorter all-pass advice resets the counter afterward; longer or equal successes and any test failures count as turns without improvement.
Each turn starts a fresh conversation with the original problem and your previous attempts, oldest first. T code is included only for the latest attempt and the most recent attempt where every T passed. You have no tools or filesystem access.

Your final response must contain only the instructions to T.
Read an integer and print its double.
